[[File:Chris Busby.jpg|thumb|Busby in 2007]]
'''Christopher Busby''' (born 1 September 1945) is a British scientist primarily studying the health effects of internal [[ionising radiation]].
Busby was a director of Green Audit Limited, a now dissolved private company which published a number of his books and papers,<ref name=greenA>{{cite web|url=https://www.greenaudit.org/|title=NEWS|last=chris|website=Green Audit, Atomic, Nuclear test veterans, Atomic test veterans, nuclear science}}</ref> and scientific advisor to the Low Level Radiation Campaign (LLRC).<ref>Green Audit, [http://www.greenaudit.org/about_green_audit.htm About Green Audit] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090805161627/http://www.greenaudit.org/about_green_audit.htm |date=5 August 2009 }}</ref>

Following the 2011 [[Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster]], Busby established a television and internet presence where he discussed the risks of [[ionizing radiation]] and the [[Japanese Government]]'s handling of the disaster. A Japanese language website marketed tests and a mineral supplement (dubbed an "anti-radiation" pill, and condemned by leading scientists as "useless") that Busby advised could mitigate the effects of ingested [[Radionuclide|radioisotopes]].<ref name=BusbyPills>{{Cite news| last = Monbiot| first = George|author2=Justin McCurry| title = Post-Fukushima 'anti-radiation' pills condemned by scientists| work = The Guardian| access-date = 22 November 2011| date = 21 November 2011| url = https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2011/nov/21/christopher-busby-radiation-pills-fukushima| location=London}}</ref>

==Career==
Busby obtained a BSc in [[Chemistry]] with [[First Class Honours]] from the [[University of London]]{{Citation needed|date=March 2025}}. He later gained a PhD in [[chemical physics]] at the [[University of Kent]], researching [[Raman spectroscopy|Raman spectro-electrochemistry]].<ref name=CERRIE>{{cite web |url=http://www.cerrie.org/people/busby.php |title=Dr Chris Bubsy (CERRIE biography) |publisher=[[Committee Examining Radiation Risks from Internal Emitters]] |access-date=1 May 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110725153513/http://www.cerrie.org/people/busby.php |archive-date=25 July 2011 }}</ref> Busby was a member of the British government sponsored [[Committee Examining Radiation Risks from Internal Emitters]] (CERRIE), which operated from 2001 to 2004.<ref name=CERRIE/> In 2001, he was appointed to the UK Ministry of Defence Oversight Committee on Depleted Uranium (DUOB).<ref name=CERRIE/> Between 2003 and 2007 he was a Fellow of the Faculty of Medicine, [[University of Liverpool]], in the Department of Human Anatomy and Cell Biology,<ref name=CERRIE/> and he was visiting professor at the School of Biomedical Sciences until his retirement in 2012 [[University of Ulster]].<ref name="ulster-busby">{{Cite web |url=http://biomed.science.ulster.ac.uk/nsb/Professor-Chris-Busby,31.html |title=Professor Chris Busby |publisher=University of Ulster |access-date=1 May 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111006144837/http://biomed.science.ulster.ac.uk/nsb/Professor-Chris-Busby,31.html |archive-date=6 October 2011 }}</ref> From 2007 to 2008 he was Guest Researcher at The Institute for Plant Nutrition and Soil Science of the Federal Agricultural Research Station in Braunschweig, Germany (FAL; from 2008 on JKI)<ref> confirmation by the then director [[Ewald Schnug]]</ref> and Jacobs University Bremen for a year and is currently Scientific Director of the private company Environmental Research SIA in Riga, Latvia. Busby is a former National Speaker on Science and Technology for the [[Green Party of England and Wales]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.greenparty.org.uk/news-archive/874.html |title=Greens launch radiation activist network |publisher=Green Party of England and Wales |date=23 October 2004 |access-date=26 January 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.greenparty.org.uk/files/reports/2004/Labour%20record%201.htm |title=Far more spin than substance |publisher=Green Party of England and Wales |date=2 September 2002 |access-date=26 January 2011}}</ref>

==Second event theory and photoelectric effect controversy==
[[File:Biphasic Curve.gif|320px|thumb|right|''The Biphasic Curve'': The cancer risk vs. radiation level in the low-dose regime (0 to 200 [[Seivert|mSv]]) for '''LNT''' and the {{Font colour|red|''' 'Biphasic Curve' '''}} promoted by Busby. {{Font colour|green|'''Background'''}} radiation is ~2.4 [[Seivert|mSv]]/year (diagram adapted by Busby from Burlakova ''et al.'' (1998)).<ref name=Burlakova1>{{Cite journal
| issn = 1342-0852
| url = http://www.rri.kyoto-u.ac.jp/NSRG/reports/kr21/kr21pdf/Burlakova.pdf
| issue = 21
| pages = 223–234
| last = Burlakova
| first = E. B.
| author2 = A. N. Goloshchapov |author3=N. V. Gorbunova |author4=S. M. Gurevich |author5=G. P. Zhizhina |author6=A. I. Kozachenko |author7=A. A. Konradov |author8=D. B. Korman |author9=E. M. Molochkina |author10=L. G. Nagler, others
| title = Peculiarities of Biological Action of Low Irradiation Doses and Their Probable Relation to the Health State of Participants of Chernobyl Accident Liquidation
| journal = Kurri Kr
| year = 1998
}}</ref>]] From 1987 onwards Busby has written on the health effects of [[ionizing radiation]] and developed what he has named "second event theory" (SET) and "photoelectric effect theory" (PET). He claims that these theories demonstrate that the widely accepted [[Linear no-threshold model|linear no-threshold (LNT)]] model substantially underestimates the risk of low level radiation (the [[Linear no-threshold model|LNT]] model is largely constructed from the 1958 to 2001 'Life Span Study' of the 120,321 [[Hibakusha|Japanese Atomic Bomb Survivors]] ({{nihongo|hibakusha|被爆者}}) who were exposed to a powerful ''external'' burst of [[neutron]] and [[Gamma ray|gamma radiation]]).<ref name=Samartzis>{{Cite journal| doi = 10.2106/JBJS.J.00256| pages = 1008–15| last = Samartzis| first = Dino| author2 = Nobuo Nishi| author3 = Mikiko Hayashi| others = John Cologne, Harry M. Cullings, Kazunori Kodama, Edward F. Miles, Sachiyo Funamoto, Akihiko Suyama, Midori Soda, Fumiyoshi Kasagi| title = Exposure to Ionizing Radiation and Development of Bone Sarcoma: New Insights Based on Atomic-Bomb Survivors of Hiroshima and Nagasaki| journal = J Bone Joint Surg Am| access-date = 30 April 2011| date = 31 March 2011| url = http://jbjs.org/article.aspx?articleID=35498| pmid = 21984980| volume = 93| issue = 11| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110606104453/http://www.jbjs.org/article.aspx?articleid=35498| archive-date = 6 June 2011| url-access = subscription}}</ref> Busby claims that in the low dose regime, radiation moderately above [[Background radiation|background]] causes more cancer than much higher levels of radiation ''i.e.'' a biphasic (bimodal) curve; a claim based on the work of Russian biologist Elena Burlakova.<ref name=Burlakova1/><ref name=Burlakova2>{{Cite book
| publisher = [[Nova Science Publishers, Inc.]]
| isbn = 978-1-56072-699-9
| pages = 11–38
| last = Burlakova 
| first = E. B.
|author2=Yu. S. Antova |author3=A. N. Goloshchapov |author4=S. M. Gurevich |author5=G. P. Zhizhina |author6=A. I. Kozachenko
 | title = Consequences of the Chernobyl Catastrophe on Human Health
| chapter = Mechanisms of biological action of low-dose irradiation
| location = New York City
| year = 1999
}}</ref>

Busby initially proposed the Second Event Theory in 1995, in his [[self-published]] book ''Wings of Death: Nuclear Pollution and Human Health''<ref name=BusbyBook>{{Cite book| publisher = Green Audit Books
| isbn = 978-1-897761-03-8
| last = Busby
| first = Chris
| title = Wings of Death: Nuclear Pollution and Human Health
| date = October 1995
| url = http://nonuclear.se/busby-wings-of-death
}}</ref> claiming that isotopes which decay sequentially, emitting two or more particles in a short [[decay chain]], have far greater genotoxic effects than predicted by the [[Linear no-threshold model|LNT]] model. According to this theory, the [[Strontium 90|<sup>90</sup>Sr-<sup>90</sup>Y]] decay chain would be ~30 times more carcinogenic than predicted by [[Linear no-threshold model|LNT]]. According to SET, primary exposure to a [[beta particle]] alters a cell to the [[G2 phase|G<sub>2</sub> Phase]], which Busby claims would render the cell highly [[Radiosensitivity|radio-sensitive]] and more prone to malignant changes when exposed to a second particle.

SET was criticised by Cox & Edwards (2000)<ref name=Cox>{{Cite journal
| issn = 0955-3002
| volume = 76
| issue = 1
| pages = 119–122
| last = Edwards
| first = A A
|author2=R Cox
| title = Commentary on the Second Event Theory of Busby
| journal = International Journal of Radiation Biology
| date = January 2000
| pmid=10665965
| doi = 10.1080/095530000139087
| s2cid = 5916027
}}</ref> who stated that if Busby's "biologically implausible" theory was correct and ''all'' irradiated cells undergo transformation to the [[G2 phase|G<sub>2</sub> Phase]], it would cause an increased risk factor of just 1.3 times and predict, on the contrary, substantial risk reduction at low doses for single emitting radioisotopes. Furthermore, it was established in 1906 (The Law of Bergonié and Tribondeau) that cells in the [[G2 phase|G<sub>2</sub> Phase]] are more resistant to radiation than cells in the [[Cell cycle#Mitotic phase (chromosome separation)|M Phase]] ([[Radiosensitivity]] and [[Cell cycle]]).<ref name=Ribondeau>{{Cite journal
| volume = 143
| pages = 983–985
| last = Ribondeau
| first = L.
|author2=J Bergonié
| title = De quelques résultats de la radiotherapie et essai de fixation d'une technique rationnelle
| journal = Comptes Rendus des Séances de l'Académie des Sciences
| year = 1906
}}</ref> The [[Committee on Medical Aspects of Radiation in the Environment|Committee Examining Radiation Risks of Internal Emitters]] (CERRIE) report, on which Busby was one of twelve members, exhaustively examined the biological plausibility of SET and commissioned an independent consultant to conduct a [[literature review]]. In 2004 CERRIE rejected the SET by a 10 to 2 majority consensus (Busby and non-scientist Richard Bramhall, dissented). The rejection was made for following reasons:<ref name=Goodhead>
{{Cite book
| publisher = London: Committee Examining Radiation Risks of Internal Emitters
| isbn = 978-0-85951-545-0
| last = Goodhead
| first = D.
| author2 = R. Bramhall
| author3 = C. Busby
| others = R. Cox, S. Darby, P. Day, J. Harrison, C. Muirhead, P. Roche, J. Simmons, others
| title = Report of the Committee Examining Radiation Risks of Internal Emitters (CERRIE)
| year = 2004
| url = http://www.cerrie.org/pdfs/cerrie_report_e-book.pdf
| access-date = 23 July 2011
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110725153420/http://www.cerrie.org/pdfs/cerrie_report_e-book.pdf
| archive-date = 25 July 2011
}}
</ref>
 
* The lack of biological plausibility for the basic preconditions of the SET
* The paucity of supporting evidence in the proponents' reviews of the SET
* The weakness of studies cited in support of the SET
* The absence of supporting evidence found by the independent review commissioned by the Committee

CERRIE also considered and rejected by 10 to 2 consensus the biphasic (bimodal) curve of Burlakova ''et al.'' (1999),<ref name=Burlakova2/> due to the study's "substantial shortcomings"; tables were so ambiguous that the risk-dose response could be interpreted as linear, biphasic or even promoting health ([[radiation hormesis]]).<ref name=Goodhead/>

In 2011, Busby began selling a [[Dissenting opinion|minority report]] for £25 on his website, in which he claimed that cancer risk from internal exposures to low doses of radiation is 300 times greater than predicted under the LNT model, that the LNT model is meaningless, and that cancer incidence rates in Sweden and Belarus increased by 40% since Chernobyl.<ref>{{Cite web
| last = Bramhall
| first = Richard
| author2 = Chris Busby
| author3 = Paul Dorfman
| title = Committee Examining Radiation Risk of Internal Emitters – MINORITY REPORT
| work = Committee Examining Radiation Risk of Internal Emitters
| date = 23 July 2011
| url = http://www.llrc.org/wobblyscience/subtopic/cerrie.htm
| access-date = 23 July 2011
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110714001141/http://www.llrc.org/wobblyscience/subtopic/cerrie.htm
| archive-date = 14 July 2011
}}</ref> His opinion on the magnitude of the cancer risk related to internal exposure to radionuclides is not consistent with the findings of analyses of lung cancer and internal exposure to alpha particles in nuclear workers.<ref> {{cite journal | journal=Epidemiology | title=Risk of lung cancer mortality in nuclear workers from internal exposure to alpha particle-emitting radionuclides | volume=28 | issue=5 | pages=675–684 | publisher=Wolters Kluwer Health | date= 2017 | doi=10.1097/EDE.0000000000000684| hdl=2445/114907 | hdl-access=free | last1=Grellier | first1=James | last2=Atkinson | first2=Will | last3=Bérard | first3=Philippe | last4=Bingham | first4=Derek | last5=Birchall | first5=Alan | last6=Blanchardon | first6=Eric | last7=Bull | first7=Richard | last8=Guseva Canu | first8=Irina | last9=Challeton-De Vathaire | first9=Cécile | last10=Cockerill | first10=Rupert | last11=Do | first11=Minh T. | last12=Engels | first12=Hilde | last13=Figuerola | first13=Jordi | last14=Foster | first14=Adrian | last15=Holmstock | first15=Luc | last16=Hurtgen | first16=Christian | last17=Laurier | first17=Dominique | last18=Puncher | first18=Matthew | last19=Riddell | first19=Anthony E. | last20=Samson | first20=Eric | last21=Thierry-Chef | first21=Isabelle | last22=Tirmarche | first22=Margot | last23=Vrijheid | first23=Martine | last24=Cardis | first24=Elisabeth | pmid=28520643 | pmc=5540354 }}</ref>

Later work by Busby focused on the health effects of ingested [[depleted uranium]] particles and the photoelectric effect theory (PET).<ref name=BusbySchnug>{{Cite book
| publisher = Margraf Publishers, Weikersheim
| isbn = 978-3-8236-1546-0
| pages = 11–22
| last = Busby
| first = C.
|author2=E. Schnug
| title = In: Loads and Fate of Fertilizer-derived Uranium
| chapter = Advanced biochemical and biophysical aspects of uranium contamination
| chapter-url = http://www.fse.org.za/downloads/ADVANCED%20BIOCHEMICAL%20AND%20BIOPHYSICAL.pdf
| year = 2008
}}</ref> The photoelectric effect theory proposes that ingested [[uranium]] particles vastly increase the potency of natural background radiation, by 500 to 1000 times, via the [[photoelectric effect|photoelectric]] effect.<ref name=pacifica>[http://www.pacifica.org/programs/dn/030131.html pacifica.org radio] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030422120222/http://pacifica.org/programs/dn/030131.html |date=22 April 2003 }}, 31 January 2003 interview with Busby, Retrieved 10 February 2008</ref><ref name=bbc>[https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/health/1422130.stm "Scientist raises new radiation fear"], news.bbc.co.uk, 5 July 2001</ref> However, subsequent computer simulations by Pattison (2013)<ref>{{Cite journal| volume = 33| issue = 1| pages = 187–198| last = Pattison| first = John E.| title = The interaction of natural background gamma radiation with depleted uranium micro-particles in the human body| journal = Journal of Radiological Protection| date = 2013| doi=10.1088/0952-4746/33/1/187| pmid = 23295360| bibcode = 2013JRP....33..187P| s2cid = 25172194}}</ref> indicate that radiation enhancement via the photoelectric effect is minute, the radiation enhancement effect due to one 10 μm-sized DU particle in 1&nbsp;cm<sup>3</sup> of tissue is just 2 in 10 million greater than a particle not being present.

== Conflicts with other low-dose radiation researchers ==
Busby is the author of two self-published books on cancer incidence in Wales, ''Wings of Death'' and ''Wolves of Water''.

The books were criticised in the ''[[Journal of Radiological Protection]]'' as "erroneous in consequence of various mistakes".<ref name=Steward2008>{{Cite journal | last1 = Steward | first1 = John A. | last2 = White | first2 = Ceri | last3 = Reynolds | first3 = Shelagh | year = 2008 | title = Leukaemia incidence in Welsh children linked with low level radiation—making sense of some erroneous results published in the media | journal = Journal of Radiological Protection | volume = 28 | pages = 33–43 | doi = 10.1088/0952-4746/28/1/001 | pmid = 18309193 | issue = 1 | bibcode = 2008JRP....28...33S | s2cid = 5134721 | url = http://herald.iop.org/jrp/m47/lt/170202/link/1417 | url-access = subscription }}{{Dead link|date=July 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref name=Wakeford2008>{{Cite journal | last = Wakeford | first = Richard | year = 2008 | title = What to believe and what not to believe | journal = Journal of Radiological Protection | volume = 28 | pages = 5–7 | doi = 10.1088/0952-4746/28/1/E03 | pmid = 18309191 | issue = 1 | doi-access = free | bibcode = 2008JRP....28....5W }}</ref> According to Richard Wakeford, the editor-in-chief of the journal, a fellow CERRIE committee member representing the nuclear industry, and a specialist in the health effects of low-dose radiation (formerly with [[British Nuclear Fuels]]),<ref>{{Cite web | title = Dr Richard Wakeford | work = Who's Who: Committee Examining Radiation Risks of Internal Emitters | publisher = CERRIE | year = 2004 | url = http://www.cerrie.org/people/wakeford.php | access-date = 14 April 2011 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110912031923/http://www.cerrie.org/people/wakeford.php | archive-date = 12 September 2011 }}</ref> Busby's work is "Deeply flawed".<ref name=Wakeford/>

Busby served on the UK Government's Committee Examining Radiation Risks of Internal Emitters (CERRIE), which operated between 2001 and 2004, and included medical professionals, scientists, delegates from [[Greenpeace]] and [[Friends of the Earth]], and Richard Wakeford representing the nuclear industry.<ref name=Wakeford>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1088/0952-4746/24/4/E02 | last1 = Wakeford | first1 = Richard | year = 2004 | title = Editorial: Reflections on CERRIE | url = http://www.iop.org/EJ/article/0952-4746/24/4/E02/jr44e1.pdf?request-id=d57be8f4-a1b0-4430-a1ca-aded182597cf | journal = Journal of Radiological Protection | volume = 24 | issue = 4| pages = 337–340 | pmid = 15682902 | bibcode = 2004JRP....24..337W | s2cid = 250804725 }}</ref> Busby ultimately disagreed with the committee's conclusions and published a "minority report" with another committee member from LLRC.<ref>{{cite news | last1 = Gould | first1 = Mark | last2 = Leake | first2 = Jonathan | url=http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/news/uk/article464333.ece | title= Nuclear Experts Gagged | publisher = Times Online | date = 1 August 2004 | access-date = 19 April 2011 | location=London}}{{dead link|date=September 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> On the LLRC website page selling the minority report, it's claimed (without citation) that north Sweden cancer rates have increased by 40% since Chernobyl.<ref>{{Cite web
  | title = Minority Report of CERRIE (flyer)
  | publisher = LLRC
  | url = http://www.llrc.org/health/subtopic/minorityflier.pdf
  | access-date = 18 April 2011
  | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110705014606/http://www.llrc.org/health/subtopic/minorityflier.pdf
  | archive-date = 5 July 2011
  }}</ref> A doctoral dissertation from 2007 was reported as saying that the area "has shown a small but statistically significant increase in the incidence of cancer".<ref>
{{Cite web
  | title = Increase in Cancer in Sweden Can Be Traced To Chernobyl
  | work = Science News
  | publisher = ScienceDaily.com
  | date = 30 May 2007
| url = https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2007/05/070530080956.htm
  | access-date = 18 April 2011
  }}  Martin Tondel, the researcher behind this work, was at last report, active with the Swedish section of International Physicians for the Prevention of Nuclear War (IPPNW). "In this capacity Dr. Tondel has visited India and Pakistan several times with International delegations arguing for nuclear disarmament in South Asia." http://www.sasnet.lu.se/environlink.html {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110616223153/http://www.sasnet.lu.se/environlink.html |date=16 June 2011 }}
</ref>

Antone Brooks (former Technical Research Director of the US Department of Energy's Low Dose Radiation Research Program)<ref name="http://nuclearstreet.com/nuclear_power_industry_news/b/nuclear_power_news/archive/2010/01/14/an-exclusive-nuclear-street-interview-with-low-dose-radiation-health-effects-expert-dr-antone-l-brooks-01142.aspx">{{cite web|last=Brooks|first=Antone|title=Dr|url=http://nuclearstreet.com/nuclear_power_industry_news/b/nuclear_power_news/archive/2010/01/14/an-exclusive-nuclear-street-interview-with-low-dose-radiation-health-effects-expert-dr-antone-l-brooks-01142.aspx|publisher=Nuclear Street|access-date=16 April 2011}}</ref> has also had differences with Busby.{{Citation needed|date=April 2011}}

==Televised comments on Fukushima I nuclear accidents==
[[File:Fukushima's Harsh Warning - Chris Busby.webm|thumb|Fukushima's Harsh Warning, Chris Busby's interview]]
In a 14 March broadcast on BBC, Busby was interviewed along with [[Ian Fells]], and characterised the accident as "exactly the same scenario" as [[Chernobyl]].  While admitting that the containment structure for [[Fukushima Dai-ichi]] was more advanced than that at Chernobyl, he claimed there could be "nuclear explosion" rather than (as reported) a hydrogen explosion, if fuel elements had [[Nuclear meltdown|melted down]] and collected at the bottom of the vessel.  He also asserted that radiation levels measured at a reactor north of Fukushima Dai-ichi (i.e. [[Onagawa Nuclear Power Plant|Onagawa]]) indicated that "up to 100 kilometers away, we are getting concentrations of plutonium, cesium and iodine" (sic – presumably radionuclides thereof) released from Fukushima Dai-ichi, making the releases comparable in his opinion to Chernobyl, in terms of human health impact.  In response to Fells' characterisation of the worst immediate effects being loss of power to an advanced industrial society, Busby said "this is a radiological catastrophe already", asserting in particular that plutonium releases were a major cause of concern.<ref name=bbc14mar2011>{{cite web|url=http://www.dailymotion.com/video/xhlgks_radiation-risk-from-nuclear-power-station-in-japan_news|title=Professor Busby gives his assessment of radiation from Fukushima nuclear reactor|work=BBC News|date=14 March 2011|access-date=14 March 2011}}</ref>

On 30 March 2011, Busby first appeared on [[RT (TV network)|RT]] (formerly known as Russia Today) stating that the [[Fukushima Nuclear Disaster]] was worse than being reported.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MognnB0g56Y|title=Full meltdown in full swing? Japan maximum nuclear alert|publisher=RT News|access-date=30 March 2011}}</ref> During the follow-up interview on 13 April 2011, Busby stated that Fukushima radiation pollution could cause up to 400,000 added cancer cases among those living within 200&nbsp;km of the reactor, with " reports of significant radiation ... even south of Tokyo".<ref>{{Cite news
  | last = Kondo
  | first = Dwight
  | title = Scientist: 400,000 Cancers Within 200 km of Fukushima Evacuation Zone
  | newspaper = Hawaiʻi News Daily
  | date = 14 April 2011
| url = http://hawaiinewsdaily.com/2011/04/scientist-predicts-400000-cancers-for-japanese-remaining-in-200-km-evacuation-zone/
  | access-date = 17 April 2011
  | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110418053303/http://hawaiinewsdaily.com/2011/04/scientist-predicts-400000-cancers-for-japanese-remaining-in-200-km-evacuation-zone/
  | archive-date = 18 April 2011
  }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S0H-mtsdsgg&feature=player_embedded|title=Busby: 400,000 to develop cancer in 200 km radius of Fukushima|website=[[YouTube]]}}</ref>

=== Controversy regarding sale of "Anti-radiation" pills ===

Following the [[Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster]], Busby established an internet presence discussing the risks of [[ionizing radiation]] and a [[conspiracy theory]] involving [[Japanese Government]]'s efforts to spread radioactive contamination throughout the country. He also marketed online, services and a [[mineral supplements|mineral supplement]] he claimed mitigate the dangers of ingested [[ionizing radiation|radioisotopes]].<ref name=BusbyPills/>

Busby claimed radioactive [[caesium-137]] released from the nuclear disaster can cause heart muscle damage and heart attacks in children and a [[mineral supplement]], sold on his Japanese language website via 4u-detox of San Pedro, California, could prevent these deleterious effects (labelled ''Busby Laboratories, Formula 1, Christopher Busby Foundation for The Children of Fukushima'').<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cbfcf.org/|title=Christopher Busby Foundation for The Children of Fukushima|website=cbfcf.org|access-date=18 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190418161732/http://cbfcf.org/|archive-date=18 April 2019}}</ref> Busby says he bases his cardiac claims on the work of husband-and-wife team [[Yury Bandazhevsky]] and Galina Bandazhevskaya; known for their controversial claims that arrhythmia and heart attacks occurred in children at [[caesium-137]] levels as low as 50 Bqkg<sup>−1</sup> and that oral apple [[pectin]] increases its excretion (by comparison [[Banana equivalent dose|banana]] contains ''ca.'' 3000 Bqkg<sup>−1</sup> of natural [[potassium-40]]).<ref name=Bandazhevskaya>{{Cite journal| volume = 134| issue = 49–50| pages = 725–729| last = Bandazhevskaya| first = GS|author2=VB Nesterenko |author3=VI Babenko |author4=IV Babenko |author5=TV Yerkovich |author6=YI Bandazhevsky | title = Relationship between Caesium (137Cs) load, cardiovascular symptoms, and source of food in "Chernobyl" children-preliminary observations after intake of oral apple pectin| journal = [[Swiss Medical Weekly]]| year = 2004| doi = 10.4414/smw.2004.10219| pmid = 15635491| doi-access = free}}</ref><ref name=Blomfield>{{Cite news| last = Blomfield| first = Adrian|author2=Adrian Blomfield| title = Chernobyl scientist warns of 'nuclear folly'| work = The Telegraph| access-date = 25 November 2011| url = https://www.telegraph.co.uk/health/healthnews/3338827/Chernobyl-scientist-warns-of-nuclear-folly.html| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20090930120838/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/health/healthnews/3338827/Chernobyl-scientist-warns-of-nuclear-folly.html| archive-date = 30 September 2009| location=London| date=24 April 2006}}</ref>

Busby later self-published a document that he claimed offered [[theory|theoretical]] support for his supplement, namely an ability to block certain radioisotopes from binding to DNA. However, his document also explains that his supplement ''cannot'' block [[caesium-137]], because it does not contain a protective dose of stable caesium: 
{{cquote|''Unfortunately, the laws prohibit the sale of such tablets despite the fact that Caesium is totally non-toxic at these levels.''<ref name=BusbySupp>{{Cite web| last = Busby| first = Chris| title = Calcium and other supplements to protect against internal radiation| date = 7 November 2011| url = https://www.scribd.com/doc/72048273/supplementrept}}</ref>}}

Note that even if the pills contained stable cesium it is unlikely that the stable cesium would increase the rate at which radioactive cesium is lost from a person. It has been shown by Prochazka ''et al.'' that the addition of stable cesium to the diet of pigs fails to increase the rate at which radioactive cesium is lost from the pigs<ref>Prochazka, H; Jandl, J; Novosad, J; [1] Neruda, O; Hejzlar, J; Spelda, S, Veterinarni Medicina (Prague), 1991, 341–348 https://www.osti.gov/etdeweb/biblio/5321449</ref>

Additionally, Busby alleges the Japanese Government is involved in a conspiracy to spread radioactive contamination throughout Japan, in an effort to hide [[cancer clusters]] from [[epidemiology|epidemiologists]] and thus hinder [[litigation]] (cancer clusters are typically statistically identified by comparison with an unexposed [[Cohort study|cohort]]).<ref name=BusbyPills/> Gerry Thomas, professor of [[molecular pathology]] at the department of surgery and cancer at [[Imperial College, London|Imperial College]], London, condemned the "anti-radiation" pills as useless and described the claims made by Busby as ludicrous. Ohtsura Niwa, professor at the [[Kyoto University]] Radiation Biology Center and CEO of BioMedics Japan, disagreed with Busby's contention that radiation is being deliberately spread throughout Japan. Niwa noted that the ownership of [[dosimeter]]s in Japan is now widespread and if [[radioactive contamination]] was actively spread about, people would know. Niwa also agreed with Thomas, that mineral supplements cannot guard against [[strontium]], [[uranium]] and [[plutonium]] [[Radionuclide|radioisotopes]]. Similar mineral supplements are widely available in chemists in Tokyo, at 1/8th cost offered by Busby Laboratories.<ref name=BusbyPills/><ref name=Monbiot>{{Cite news| last = Monbiot| first = George| title = Christopher Busby's wild claims hurt green movement and Green party| work = The Guardian| access-date = 22 November 2011| date = 22 November 2011| url = https://www.theguardian.com/environment/georgemonbiot/2011/nov/22/christopher-busby-nuclear-green-party| location=London}}</ref>

In 2008, a research team at the Experimental Radio-TOXological Laboratory (LRTOX), France, independently investigated the effects of high level (500 Bqkg<sup>−1</sup>) [[caesium-137]] exposure in animals (heart, testes, blood, cholesterol, immune system, foetus etc.). For example, Guéguen ''et al.'' (2008) investigated the possible cardiac effects of 500 Bqkg<sup>−1</sup> caesium-137 exposure in rats over 3 months. They observed that, while [[caesium-137]] exposure did not cause any damage to heart cells or arrhythmias, results indicated that quite subtle cardiac impairment might worsen in some sensitive individuals over time.<ref name="Guéguen">{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1007/s12012-008-9013-3| issn = 1530-7905| volume = 8| pages = 33–40| last = Guéguen| first = Yann| author2 = Philippe Lestaevel |author3=Line Grandcolas |others=Cédric Baudelin, Stéphane Grison, Jean-René Jourdain, Patrick Gourmelon, Maâmar Souidi| title = Chronic Contamination of Rats with 137Cesium Radionuclide: Impact on the Cardiovascular System| journal = Cardiovascular Toxicology| date = 8 March 2008| pmid = 18327657| issue = 1| s2cid = 24085449}}</ref> Also, Le Gal ''et al.'' (2006) found that the excretion of [[caesium-137]] was not increased by oral apple [[pectin]], however [[prussian blue]] (the drug [[Radiogardase]]) enhanced faecal excretion of caesium-137 fivefold.<ref name=LeGall>{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1016/j.biochi.2006.09.010| issn = 0300-9084| volume = 88| issue = 11| pages = 1837–1841|last = Le Gall| first = B.| author2 = F. Taran |author3=D. Renault |author4=J.-C. Wilk |author5=E. Ansoborlo| title = Comparison of prussian blue and apple-pectin efficacy on 137Cs decorporation in rats| journal = Biochimie| date = November 2006| pmid = 17069947}}</ref> Furthermore, the study of Bandazhevskaya (2004) involving oral apple [[pectin]] was criticised by Jargin (2010), who highlighted a number of serious flaws that meant the claims made could not substantiated.<ref name=Jargin>{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1007/s00411-010-0313-1| issn = 0301-634X| volume = 49| pages = 743–745| last = Jargin| first = Sergei V.| title = Overestimation of Chernobyl consequences: poorly substantiated information published| journal = Radiation and Environmental Biophysics| date = 17 July 2010| issue = 4| pmid = 20640449| bibcode = 2010REBio..49..743J| s2cid = 40800641}}</ref>

Claiming that a supplement can be of use in the "''cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of disease''" renders it equivalent to a drug and subject to oversight by the US [[Food and Drug Administration]] (FDA) (Section 201(g)(1) of the 1938 [[Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act]]). Specifically, drugs must be demonstrated to work and proven safe. In April 2011, the [[Food and Drug Administration|FDA]] sent warning letters to an unrelated company, Premier Micronutrient Corporation of Nashville, Tennessee, US, who similarly claim that its "anti-oxidant" supplements are capable of preventing illness caused by radiation (''Bioshield-Radiation R1'' and ''Bioshield Radiation R2''). The [[Food and Drug Administration|FDA]] pointed out there was no scientific data demonstrating the drugs safety or effectiveness in treating radiation exposure.<ref name=FDAWarningLetter>{{Cite web| title = Warning Letters – Premier Micronutrient Corporation 4/28/11| website = [[Food and Drug Administration]]| format = WebContent| access-date = 24 November 2011| url = https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/ucm253423.htm| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110506074743/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/ucm253423.htm| archive-date = 6 May 2011}}</ref> However, ''Bioshield Radiation R2'' subsequently resumed sale with a legal waver, "''These statements have not been evaluated by the Food and Drug Administration. This product is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease.''"; that it is a [[Dietary supplement|food supplement]].<ref name=FDA_Sup>{{Cite web| last = U.S. Food and Drug Administration| title = Consumer Information – Overview of Dietary Supplements| website = [[Food and Drug Administration]]| format = WebContent| access-date = 24 November 2011| url = https://www.fda.gov/food/dietarysupplements/consumerinformation/ucm110417.htm| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20090603045226/http://www.fda.gov/Food/DietarySupplements/ConsumerInformation/ucm110417.htm| archive-date = 3 June 2009}}</ref> The [[Food and Drug Administration|FDA]] approves three over-the-counter drugs for [[iodine-131]] and one [[prescription drug]] (Radiogardase) for caesium-137 contamination.<ref name=FDA_Cs137>{{Cite web| last = Research| first = Center for Drug Evaluation and| title = Bioterrorism and Drug Preparedness – FDA Approves First New Drug Application for Treatment of Radiation Contamination due to Cesium or Thallium (10/2/2003)| website = [[Food and Drug Administration]]| format = WebContent| access-date = 25 November 2011| url = https://www.fda.gov/Drugs/EmergencyPreparedness/BioterrorismandDrugPreparedness/ucm130335.htm}}{{dead link|date=May 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref><ref name=FTC>{{Cite web
| last = U.S. FTC
| title = FTC Warns Consumers About Scam Artists' Pitch for Potassium Iodide Treatment
| work = Federal Trade Commission
| format = Government
| date = 21 March 2011
| url = http://www.ftc.gov/opa/2011/03/iodide.shtm
}}</ref>

==Research on weapons derived uranium==

Busby has written and spoken about the potential health effects of [[depleted uranium]].<ref>''Depleted Science: the health consequences and mechanisms of exposure to fallout from Depleted Uranium weapons'' in ''The Trojan Horses of Nuclear War'' M. Kuepker and D. Kraft eds. Hamburg, 2004</ref><ref>''Depleted Uranium Weapons, metal particles and radiation dose'' European J. Biology and Bioelectromagnetics 2005, 1(1) 82–93</ref><ref>''Does uranium contamination amplify natural background radiation dose to the DNA?'' European J. Biology and Bioelectromagnetics 2005, 1(2) 120–131</ref><ref>''Depleted Uranium. Why all the fuss?'' United Nations Disarmament Forum Journal UNIDIR, Nov 2008</ref><ref>"Science on Trial: On the Biological Effects and Health Risks following exposure to aerosols produced by the use of DU weapons" Invited presentation to the Royal Society, London 19 July 2000 (also given at the Int. Conference against DU, Manchester, 4 Nov.) and on "Health effects of Depleted Uranium (again)" in 2001</ref><ref>{{YouTube|dOI-wpMlq28|Dr Chris Busby at the Royal Society: Scientific Dishonesty}}</ref>  He has claimed that people have been exposed to uranium during the 2nd Gulf War (2003),<ref>[http://www.mindfully.org/Nucs/2006/DU-Europe-Contamination1jan06.htm Did the use of uranium weapons in Gulf War 2 result in contamination of Europe?] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120810005926/http://www.mindfully.org/Nucs/2006/DU-Europe-Contamination1jan06.htm |date=10 August 2012 }} Chris Busby and Saoirse Morgan; 1 March 2006, ''European J. Biology and Bioelectromagnetics''</ref> [[1995 NATO bombing campaign in Bosnia and Herzegovina|the Bosnia campaign]] (1996),<ref>[http://www.euradcom.org/publications/ecrruraniumrept.pdf Uranium and Health: The Health Effects of Exposure to Uranium and Uranium Weapons Fallout] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111104145155/http://www.euradcom.org/publications/ecrruraniumrept.pdf |date=4 November 2011 }} Chris Busby; Documents of the ECRR 2010 No 2</ref><ref>Ballardie FW, Cowley R, Cox A, Curry A, Denley H, Denton J, Dick J, Gerquin-Kern J-L, Redmond A, ''A man who brought the war home with him'' The Lancet, Vol. 372 No. 9653 p 1926</ref> and in the [[2006 Israel-Lebanon war]].<ref>[http://www.llrc.org/du/subtopic/lebanrept.pdf Busby C, Williams D, ''Evidence of Enriched Uranium in guided weapons employed by the Israeli Military in Lebanon in July 2006''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120426072051/http://www.llrc.org/du/subtopic/lebanrept.pdf |date=26 April 2012 }} Research Note 6/2006 Aberystwyth: Green Audit (accessed 20 September 2014)</ref><ref>[http://www.llrc.org/du/subtopic/ambulance.pdf Busby, Chris and Williams, Dai, ''Further Evidence of Enriched Uranium in guided weapons employed by the Israeli Military in Lebanon in July 2006: Ambulance Air Filter Analysis''] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121224200811/http://www.llrc.org/du/subtopic/ambulance.pdf |date=24 December 2012 }} Green Audit Research Note 7/2006. 3 November 2006</ref> However, a study by the [[United Nations Environment Programme]] did not find any traces of depleted uranium in weapons used during the 2006 Israel-Lebanon war.<ref>[https://news.un.org/en/story/2006/11/198902-israel-did-not-use-depleted-uranium-during-conflict-hizbollah-un-agency-finds United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP): "Israel did not use depleted uranium during conflict with Hizbollah, UN agency finds" 8 November 2006]</ref>

A review of past studies of birth defects in Iraq concluded that there was no clear increase in birth defects and no clear indication of a possible environmental exposure including depleted uranium.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Al-Hadithi|first=T.|author2=J. Al-Diwan|author3=A. Saleh|author4=N. Shabila|year=2012|title=Birth defects in Iraq and the plausibility of environmental exposure: a review|journal=Conflict and Health|volume=6|issue=1|page=3|doi=10.1186/1752-1505-6-3|pmc=3492088|pmid=22839108 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

In November 2012, Busby gave a talk in Geneva at the [[Human Rights Council]]<!-- 's session 'Roundtable on Human Rights Issues that Require the Council's Attention: Iraq.' --><ref>[http://www.canadafreepress.com/index.php/article/49520 Obama-backed UN "Human Rights" Council Facilitates US-bashing Meet] by Anne Bayefsky</ref> about the failures of radiation protection as a human rights issue.<ref>[http://justiceforiraq.blogspot.co.at/2012/09/press-release.html Birth Defects study in Fallujah Iraq] (Press release)</ref>

==Arrest under the Explosives Substances Act (1883)==

He was arrested in 2018 in Devon after the [[nerve agent]] attack on the [[skripal affair|Skripals]] when some police officers visited his home after reports that his 29-year-old housemate was acting in a strange manner. He was not arrested in connection with the nerve agent attack but after two police officers felt unwell in his house.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-devon-45516797|title = Bideford radiation expert held over home chemicals|work = BBC News|date = 13 September 2018}}</ref> He was arrested under the [[Explosive Substances Act 1883]] before being released later. Chris Busby did state that he had a bottle of [[nitric acid]] somewhere in the house. Chris Busby expressed the view that his arrest and the search of his home were a retaliation against him for his work on nuclear matters.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/uk-news/inside-backroom-chemical-lab-73-13247967|title=Inside the backroom chemical lab that sparked a bomb scare - in Devon|website=[[Daily Mirror]]|date=14 September 2018}}</ref> The possession of nitric acid is regulated by the [[Control_of_Poisons_and_Explosives_Precursors_Regulations_2023|Control of Poisons and Explosives Precursors Regulations 2015]] when the concentration of the nitric acid is above 3%. An aqueous solution which is 3% nitric acid is ''circa'' 0.7 M.

==Relocation to Latvia==

Chris Busby has relocated to [[Latvia]] and the author information on his paper on the epidemiology of cancer risks associated with service aboard a nuclear powered ship ([[USS Ronald Reagan]]) indicates his address to be [[Riga]]. His paper argues that there is a higher rate of cancer in the workers on the ship than there are in other US Navy Personnel.<ref>C. Busby, Cancer Investigation, 2020, volume 38, issue 3, pages 143-149</ref>

In recent times Chris Busby has published a paper on the [[origins of life]] where he considers [[entropy]] and [[Maxwell's demon]], he argues that the phosphate mineral [[apaitite]] was involved in the creation of the first life forms.<ref>Christopher Busby and Charles Vyvyan Howard, Advances in Biological Chemistry, 2017, volume 7, pages 170-181.</ref>
